subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: Help me understand what's worth attention in these incident descriptions.

judge.implied_focus: Which incident topics/themes warrant analyst attention (attention-worthiness derived from incident short_description)

per_column.name: topic
per_column.rationale: Infers the semantic theme of each incident from its description, establishing the categorical basis of 'what' the incident is about -- the core substrate for identifying what's worth attention.

per_column.name: is_high_frequency_topic
per_column.rationale: Derives whether a topic is common vs. rare, a facet of attention (volume-driven prioritization) that builds directly on the topic dimension.

per_column.name: attention_flag
per_column.rationale: Directly operationalizes the attention-worthiness concept into a graded signal (Routine/Medium/High/Low-Anomaly), which is the explicit target the query asks about.

judge.rationale: The three columns centre coherently on a single inferable focus: attention-worthiness of incidents grounded in their descriptive topic. 'topic' extracts the theme, 'is_high_frequency_topic' adds a volume facet, and 'attention_flag' synthesizes the priority signal -- a sound theme -> frequency -> attention structure rather than a grab-bag. Structure is slightly weakened because 'is_high_frequency_topic' is a coarse binary largely redundant with topic frequency, and 'attention_flag' bundles anomaly and severity into one label without exposing its drivers, limiting analytical granularity. Still, the implied focus is genuinely actionable: an analyst can triage High/Low-Anomaly incidents and investigate high-frequency topics, so it is neither vacuous nor a mere restatement. It is derived from real content (descriptions) rather than mechanical text metrics.
